_comment: ADDITIVE IONO LADDER, arm A1 (2026-08-03) - SH truncation degree 8 -> 15.
WHY THE qz0 SUBSTRATE.  Queue P3's SUBTRACTIVE iono ladder (layer2 off / mech-B off /
sigma_rep 5 -> 50) was a COMPLETE NULL on the qz=1e-4 posture: every arm moved mature
steps < 1 % and total_IF within noise.  P2 explains why: at qz=1e-4 the carried-DD walk
IS q_z (mature steps 0.953/0.789/0.485 cyc/ep, structure function still growing to k=32),
so it swamps any iono-representation term.  On pdfix_qz0 the walk collapses to
0.168/0.096/0.030 cyc/ep and the SF FLATTENS (k=32: 21.15 -> 1.51).  What remains at that
floor is the representation residual - which is the only substrate on which an ADDITIVE
iono change is visible at all.
qz0 IS A DIAGNOSTIC SUBSTRATE, NOT A POSTURE.  P2 graded it a FAIL on the card's own
stated rule: total_IF worst_med +16.4 %, worst_max +24.3 %, clk_std 4.86 -> 5.29 (+8.8 %)
= a clock-QC degradation.  The mechanism is that q_z decides whether the iono
mismodelling lands in the carried DDs (walk) or in the sat clocks / code biases
(total_IF).  So a WIN HERE IS NOT A POSTURE DECISION: any arm that wins on qz0 must be
re-run on the qz=1e-4 posture (control runs/pdfix_v3) before it can be promoted.
THE ONE VARIABLE: estimation.global_vtec_sh.max_degree 8 -> 15.  Layer 2 stays at
degree 4, mech-B v3k stays on, representation_sigma_tecu stays 5.0.
OUTSIDE THE LEDGER'S ENVELOPE, DELIBERATELY.  The POSTURE ledger's deg-15 evidence line
(GnssConfigNetworkPosture.cpp) is conditioned on n_sta >= 150 AND an iono cutoff >= 25 deg
(sat code-OSB drift 0.66 vs 2.31 m, epoch step 1.57 vs 4.43 cm).  This lineage meets the
cutoff (ionosphere_weighting.elevation_cutoff_deg = 25.0) but NOT the station count: 63
stations, GPS-only.  Degree 15 is 256 layer-1 coefficients against roughly 500-600 LOS per
epoch - about 2 LOS per coefficient, thin, and regularized only by the Kaula prior
(kaula_scale_tecu 10.0, q_per_degree 0.01).  That thinness is the POINT of the arm: the
question is whether a finer surface earns its parameters at THIS density or aliases.
GRADE (all datum-invariant, standing invariant #5; control = runs/pdfix_qz0):
1. scripts/grade_dd_spillway.py - mature steps by age and the STRUCTURE FUNCTION.  The
qz0 floor is 0.168/0.096/0.030 cyc/ep with SF k=32 = 1.51.  A real iono win pushes
the floor DOWN; anything else is noise at this scale.
2. CROSS-BAND RATIO - the discriminator.  Every arm of P2/P3 including qz0 sits at
1.263-1.265 against the common-cycle signature 1.2833, i.e. the residual's DIRECTION
never changed, only its magnitude.  If degree 15 is genuinely absorbing iono, this
ratio must MOVE AWAY from 1.2833.  If it does not, the extra coefficients are not
eating iono no matter what the step numbers do.
3. ALIASING WATCH (the documented failure mode): the SH a00 band, the sh_health gate
engagements/withholds, and the iono-deweight engage count.  A finer surface with too
few LOS pushes power into low-degree coefficients and the a00 band is where that
shows first.
4. scripts/chain_stability.py total_IF hr2 + clk_std - the no-harm check, read against
the qz0 control (NOT against pdfix_v3: qz0 already carries the +16.4 % / clk_std 5.29
degradation, so the question here is whether degree 15 makes it better or worse).
5. scripts/parse_carry_psd.py - the PD gate still has to pass; degree 15 changes the
conditioning of the shared block the DD fold rides on.
6. Perf: (N+1)^2 coefficients means 81 -> 256, so the shared system grows.  Note the
cost; it is not a gate at 63 sta.
